p: The eastern side of the Dean has a strong industrial story to tell, and it's well worth digging into once you're back on solid ground. The Dean Heritage Centre at Soudley explores the forest's history, from its free miners to its woodland crafts, and Hopewell Colliery gives you the chance to see a real free mine and learn how coal was worked in the forest for centuries.

Closer to the lake, Cannop Ponds are a peaceful pair of old mill ponds surrounded by trees, lovely for spotting ducks and other wildlife and a gentle place to sit after a busy morning. Keen cyclists can also pick up the forest's popular family cycle trail, which loops through the woods on old railway lines and is easy on the legs.

For the treetop session, plan on a couple of hours once you're harnessed up, and arrive in good time, because country lanes in the Dean can be slower than the sat nav thinks. If you're going in summer, a morning slot keeps you out of the warmest part of the day.

One handy hint: pack a towel or a change of top in the car. Between the climbing, the scrambling and the odd sweaty moment on a high crossing, you'll appreciate feeling fresh for the drive home or a meal out in one of the forest towns like Coleford or Lydney.
